verdict.rationale: Manufact documents connecting any external MCP server by pasting its URL, and it then connects to that server directly for its Chat, testing, and publish workflows. It also runs servers across different MCP clients and models. That is genuine client-side MCP consumption, but it is framed around testing and publishing your own server rather than a general agent that uses plugged-in tools. Manufact's own MCP server (docs-14) is server-side and does not count toward this story. Missing for 10: documentation of how Chat discovers and invokes the connected server's tools, support for using multiple servers' tools together in general agent workflows, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: paste your MCP URL. No deploy required: Manufact connects directly for Chat, testing, and the publish workflow.
Already hosting an MCP server elsewhere? On New Server, scroll to Connect an existing server and paste your MCP URL. No deploy required
Manufact executes them across different MCP clients and LLM models, because a server that works in one client can still fail in another.
